response: Yes, biomolecular identification of allergenic pollen offers a new perspective for aerobiological monitoring. Traditional methods of pollen identification rely on morphological characteristics, which can be time-consuming and require specialized expertise. Biomolecular techniques, such as DNA sequencing and PCR (polymerase chain reaction), can provide rapid and accurate identification of pollen species, allowing for more effective monitoring and management of airborne allergens. This approach can also help to detect hidden allergens, improve pollen counting accuracy, and enhance our understanding of pollen allergenicity, ultimately benefiting public health and allergy sufferers.
